section_about:
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to own actuator development and integration from system goals through production readiness.
The actuator program spans mechanical, electrical, firmware, harnessing, controls, test, reliability, manufacturing, and supply chain, and needs a TPM who can turn cross-functional decisions into clear scope, executable milestones, and timely decisions.
In this role, you will help the team converge on the right technical plan, surface risks early, and deliver reliable actuator systems on schedule.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.
section_responsibilities:
- Drive actuator programs end-to-end, aligning scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria across engineering teams.
- Drive scope lock and technical convergence for sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals while connecting component decisions to system performance.
- Coordinate actuator development across motors, gears, sensing, electronics, and firmware, and align the electrical and mechanical interfaces that connect actuators to the broader robot.
- Lead validation planning from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.
- Drive tradeoff decisions across cost, quality, performance, schedule, and lead time by collaborating cross-functionally and quantifying impact to meet program deliverables.
- Establish effective mechanisms for technical reviews, change control, design releases, decision tracking, and manufacturing readiness.
- Surface risks early and drive decisions, owners, and actions to closure.
- Cross-functional scope, milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and exit criteria are aligned across engineering, supply chain and manufacturing teams.
- Sprints, MVPs, and stretch goals converge on decisions connected to system performance.
- Validation is planned from early prototypes through engineering validation, reliability testing, and production readiness.
- Risks, tradeoffs, owners, and actions are surfaced early and driven to closure to meet program deliverables.
- Mitigation strategies are well communicated and aligned upon, acceleration of hardware development from design to trials on the floor is quantifiable.
- Tools and workflows built are well embedded in the daily routine of all the team members, thus do not seem an added overhead to get things done.

Our Sales team has a unique mission to help customers understand the deep impact that highly capable AI models can bring to their business and users.
This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and value-driven strategy.
You'll be a key driver of new business opportunities through the entire sales cycle, from pipeline generation to closure.
You'll work with researchers, engineers, and solution strategists to help customers evolve their industry with AI.
This role can be based in our San Francisco, New York, or Seattle offices.
We are also considering applications to work remotely from within the U.S.

- Closely monitor the industry landscape (people, competitors, partners, etc.) to contribute to product roadmap and other corporate strategies

- Working directly with c-level executives

section_about:
OpenAI's Financial Engineering (FinEng) team powers how revenue flows through our products-pricing & packaging, checkout, payments, subscriptions, and the financial infrastructure behind them.
We operate at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Risk, Finance, and Go-to-Market to ensure that paying for OpenAI products is seamless, reliable, scalable, and globally optimized.
As OpenAI expands internationally and across product surfaces, FinEng plays a critical role in enabling durable, efficient revenue growth.
As a Data Scientist for Financial Engineering, you will drive the measurement, experimentation, and optimization work that powers OpenAI's monetization infrastructure.
You will define how we measure and improve checkout, payments, subscriptions, and pricing systems globally-balancing conversion, risk, cost, reliability, and user experience.
As a senior individual contributor, you will establish source-of-truth metrics, design rigorous experiments, develop analytical frameworks, and translate complex findings into decisions that directly affect revenue and international growth.
We use a hybrid model of three days per week in the office and offer relocation support.
section_responsibilities:
- Define key metrics and guardrails across checkout, payments, subscriptions, and pricing.
- Design experiments, staged rollouts, and offline incrementality studies.
- Improve conversion, payment performance, retention, and involuntary churn.
- Develop pricing, elasticity, FX, and localization frameworks.
- Partner with Data Engineering to build trusted datasets and operational monitoring.
- Turn complex analysis into recommendations that shape product and business decisions.
- Provide technical leadership and mentor other data scientists.
section_requirements:
- 10+ years of experience in data science, experimentation, or product analytics.
- Experience with monetization, payments, checkout, subscriptions, or pricing.
- Advanced SQL and Python skills and strong expertise in experimentation and causal inference.
- A track record of independently leading high-impact, cross-functional analytical work.
- Strong product judgment, communication skills, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

location: San Francisco; New York City; US - Remote
section_about:
Across industries, OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering (AIE) team helps organizations turn frontier AI into safe, reliable production systems that deliver meaningful business outcomes.
We work directly with customers' engineering, product, security, and transformation teams to navigate complex architectures, data environments, governance requirements, and organization-wide change.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better OpenAI products and reusable patterns that help customers move faster.
As an Enterprise AIE, you will serve as a technical partner to leading organizations including universities and other educational institutions, helping them turn ambitious AI use cases into durable production systems and adoption at scale.
You will combine deep technical judgment with hands-on engineering to provide technical leadership on complex customer deployments.
You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions about model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness.
Success is measured by durable production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful business impact.
Your deployment experience will also directly influence how OpenAI's products evolve.
This role may be based in one of our offices in New York City or San Francisco, or it may be performed remotely.
Office-based employees follow a hybrid work model with three days per week in the office.
We offer relocation assistance to new employees.
section_responsibilities:
- Work hands-on in code to design, build, evaluate, and deploy AI systems from prototype to reliable production and scaled adoption that solve important customer problems and deliver measurable business outcomes.
- Partner with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and success criteria.
- Make sound technical decisions across model selection, agent and tool design, retrieval, context design, data pipelines, evaluation, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers to resolution.
- Partner closely with customers' engineering teams and OpenAI's Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Go-to-Market teams to turn deployment experience into actionable product feedback.
- Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.
section_requirements:
- Have personally designed, built, and shipped AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, taking them from prototype to production and making substantial contributions through coding, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering.
Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.
- Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working end to end across model APIs, agent and tool development, retrieval and data pipelines, evaluation, observability, integrations, and production operations.
Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
- Know how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, automated graders, production signals, and human judgment.
- Have navigated enterprise production requirements, including integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
- Experience navigating education or research environments, including institutional data, privacy, access controls and complex integrations, is valuable.
- Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
- Communicate clearly and credibly with hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security and product teams, and executives.
- Take end-to-end ownership, exercise strong technical judgment, and move effectively through ambiguity.
- Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility.
Experience working with education institutions, particularly universities, is preferred but not required.
Prior OpenAI product experience is not required.

section_about:
OpenAI's Professional Services team helps organizations move from AI ambition to durable production outcomes.
We partner with customers on complex deployments and build the strategy, commercial models, operating mechanisms, and delivery capacity needed to realize value from OpenAI's models and products.
The team works across Go-to-Market, Forward Deployed Engineering, Technical Success, Finance, Product, Legal, Data, Systems, and delivery partners.
We are building a services motion that is customer-centered, commercially rigorous, operationally scalable, and deliberately connected to product adoption.
We are seeking a senior GTM Strategy & Operations professional to build and scale the operating system for OpenAI's Professional Services business.
This is a foundational, hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of business strategy, finance, go-to-market, and delivery.
You will turn ambiguous questions-what we offer, how we price and package it, how we plan capacity, and how we measure performance-into clear decisions and repeatable mechanisms.
You will own business planning, pricing and packaging, forecasting and modeling, management reporting, and cross-functional strategic initiatives.
You will build integrated views of demand, staffing, revenue, margin, and delivery performance; replace one-off analyses with durable processes; and create operating cadences that help leaders act early.
You will be a trusted partner to Professional Services, GTM, FDE, Technical Success, Finance, Product, Legal, Revenue Operations, and Data leaders.
The right person combines direct Professional Services judgment with rigorous analytics, executive communication, and the willingness to build the model, process, or dashboard themselves.
section_responsibilities:
- Define and drive the business and GTM strategy for Professional Services, including target customer needs, offer portfolio, positioning, pricing and packaging, partner motions, and where to standardize versus tailor delivery.
- Own long-range, annual, and quarterly planning for the services business, translating goals into bookings, revenue, margin, capacity, utilization, role mix, geography, hiring, and investment assumptions.
- Build and maintain integrated demand, capacity, staffing, and revenue models; develop scenarios and sensitivities; improve bottom-up forecast accuracy; and turn the output into clear executive recommendations.
- Design the management system for the business: KPIs, source-of-truth reporting, dashboards, pipeline and staffing reviews, and monthly and quarterly operating cadences.
- Improve the end-to-end services lifecycle from opportunity intake and scoping through commercial design, contracting, staffing, delivery, and expansion, partnering with Revenue Operations and Systems rather than duplicating their ownership.
- Partner with Finance, Legal, GTM, FDE, Technical Success, and delivery leaders on business cases, services economics, deal tradeoffs, resource allocation, and investment decisions.
- Lead ambiguous cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through implementation, creating clear decision rights, mechanisms, and accountability.
- Translate recurring customer and delivery patterns into inputs for product strategy, enablement, partner strategy, and more repeatable product-plus-services offerings that accelerate durable product adoption.
section_requirements:
- 8+ years of experience in GTM Strategy & Operations, Business Operations, Strategic Finance, management consulting, or a comparable role, including direct experience in a technology Professional Services, implementation, systems-integration, consulting, or managed-services business.
- Deep command of services economics and operating levers such as pipeline, bookings, backlog, revenue timing, gross margin, utilization, capacity, staffing mix, delivery quality, and customer outcomes.
- Exceptional quantitative modeling skills: you can build auditable demand, staffing, revenue, and scenario models; work fluently in spreadsheets; and use SQL, BI, or other data tools to test assumptions and improve decisions.
- Strong commercial and GTM judgment across pricing and packaging, offer design, forecasting, resource allocation, and complex enterprise delivery motions.
- A record of turning ambiguous strategy into repeatable operating mechanisms, decision frameworks, reporting rhythms, and measurable results.
- Excellent executive communication and influence; you can frame choices, surface assumptions, and drive alignment across technical and non-technical leaders.
- Demonstrated leadership of complex cross-functional programs and teams.
People-management experience is helpful, but this role is initially scoped as a senior individual contributor.
- A low-ego, high-ownership working style, comfort with rapid change, and genuine interest in how frontier AI can create durable customer value.

section_about:
The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact.
We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption.
The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.
Within the team, Partner Applied AI Architects work with strategic partners-including global and regional system integrators, consulting and advisory firms, and technology partners-to extend OpenAI's technical reach and help partners deliver high-quality AI solutions for our joint customers.
We bring together technical strategy, partner enablement, architecture expertise, and practical deployment experience, working closely with Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and specialist delivery teams.
As a Partner Applied AI Architect, you will be a senior technical advisor to a portfolio of strategic partners and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership and delivery organizations.
You will shape how partners build practices around OpenAI, develop solutions using our products, and take joint customers from AI opportunity and technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable business impact.
You will own the technical strategy and architecture across partner engagements involving ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions.
In close partnership with the Revenue Partnerships team, you will translate joint business priorities into technical strategies, solution patterns, enablement plans, and a focused portfolio of high-value customer opportunities.
You will work directly with partners on strategic customer engagements-leading discovery, shaping architectures, navigating complex technical decisions, and helping secure technical wins-while building the partner capabilities required to deliver successfully and independently at scale.
You will remain accountable for the technical quality and outcomes of the partnership while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, security, product, enablement, and other teams when deeper expertise is needed.
The role calls for strong architectural judgment, executive presence, partner leadership, and the ability to move confidently between business strategy and hands-on technical conversations.
section_responsibilities:
- Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a portfolio of strategic partners, building trusted relationships with their executives, AI leaders, architects, engineering teams, and delivery organizations.
- Partner closely with the Revenue Partnerships team as one virtual team, aligning partner strategy, technical priorities, joint customer opportunities, and measures of success.
- Develop the technical strategy and plan for each partner, identifying priority solutions, use cases, technical capabilities, enablement needs, delivery risks, and opportunities to drive customer adoption.
- Assess prospective and existing partners' technical capabilities and delivery readiness, identifying strengths, gaps, and the investments required to successfully deliver OpenAI-powered solutions.
- Lead technical discovery with partners and joint customers to identify, qualify, and prioritize AI use cases tied to meaningful business outcomes.
- Develop clear Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, enterprise data, integrations, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.
- Collaborate with partner sales and technical teams on strategic opportunities, providing technical guidance through discovery, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, architectural recommendations, and proofs of value.
- Guide partners through their initial and most strategic OpenAI deployments, helping them navigate technical tradeoffs and production dependencies while ensuring solutions meet a high bar for quality, security, reliability, and responsible deployment.
- Build partner capability and technical self-sufficiency through tailored enablement, architectural guidance, reusable solution patterns, technical workshops, and mentorship.
- Establish clear standards and mechanisms for partner-delivered solution quality, identifying risks early and intervening when architecture, implementation, security, evaluation, or adoption issues threaten customer outcomes.
- Orchestrate the right OpenAI specialists across Deployment Engineering, Product, Security, implementation, enablement, and domain teams while maintaining clear ownership and handoffs between OpenAI and partner delivery teams.
- Track partner capability, joint pipeline technical progress, production adoption, usage, solution quality, and measurable customer impact to identify where additional investment or intervention is needed.
- Identify repeatable patterns across partner engagements and turn them into architectures, playbooks, reference solutions, and best practices that allow successful approaches to scale across partners and customers.
- Bring insights from partners and joint customers back to Product, Engineering, Research, and Partnerships, helping shape product strategy, technical guidance, and the broader OpenAI partner ecosystem.

section_about:
OpenAI's Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) team partners across the company to enable safe, responsible growth.
This role will be a senior EHS partner to our robotics operations as our operating footprint expands.
You will work closely with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and external partners to integrate safety into how our facilities are designed, built, staffed, and operated.
We are seeking a Senior Manager, EHS - Robotics to provide senior, hands-on safety leadership across multiple sites.
This role is for an experienced EHS leader who can operate independently in a fast-moving technical environment, anticipate risk before it becomes an incident, and build practical safety systems that scale with the business.
Our robotics operations are scaling quickly, with a growing mix of construction, commissioning, workforce expansion, and around-the-clock operations.
This creates a complex and evolving risk environment and requires strong preventive planning, consistent field presence, and sustained incident-management oversight.
This leader will own site-level EHS strategy and execution for the robotics portfolio while partnering with the broader EHS team on company-wide standards and programs.
The successful candidate will look around corners: planning for future ramps, identifying requirements early, influencing design and operating decisions, and creating durable systems that enable teams to move quickly without compromising safety.
section_responsibilities:
- Serve as a senior EHS partner across robotics R&D operations, owning site-level safety strategy, priorities, and execution as the footprint scales.
- Anticipate EHS requirements for new operations, equipment, processes, construction phases, staffing ramps, and 24/7 operations, and translate them into practical plans before work begins.
- Lead proactive risk identification and control across robotics activities, including machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and other site-specific risks.
- Build and maintain site EHS programs, risk assessments, procedures, training, inspections, corrective-action systems, emergency preparedness, and compliance processes appropriate to each site's risk profile.
- Partner with Robotics, Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Workplace, Construction, Security, People, Legal, and vendors to embed safety into facility design, equipment deployment, work planning, and operating decisions.
- Provide visible field leadership across shifts and operating conditions, establishing mechanisms that support effective EHS coverage and escalation for 24/7 operations.
- Lead incident response and investigation for significant events; ensure timely fact-finding, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, verification, trend analysis, and communication of lessons learned.
- Use incident, near-miss, inspection, and operational data to identify recurring risks and drive preventive actions across sites rather than addressing events in isolation.
- Oversee contractor and contingent-worker safety interfaces, clarifying responsibilities, expectations, reporting, and corrective-action ownership across multi-employer worksites.
- Maintain strong regulatory compliance and readiness, including applicable Cal/OSHA and OSHA requirements, while developing metrics and reporting that make site risks, actions, and performance visible to leadership.
section_requirements:
- 15+ years of progressive EHS experience, including significant leadership responsibility in robotics, advanced manufacturing, R&D, industrial, or similarly complex technical environments.
- Strong technical knowledge across occupational safety and health, with depth in areas such as machine safety, ergonomics, electrical safety, hazardous energy, material handling, hazardous materials, contractor safety, and incident investigation.
- Demonstrated experience supporting complex sites through rapid scale, construction and operational overlap, commissioning, process change, or transition to extended or 24/7 operations.
- Strong working knowledge of OSHA and Cal/OSHA requirements and the ability to translate regulatory obligations into practical, scalable operating programs.
- Demonstrated success influencing senior technical and operational leaders, especially where EHS does not directly own the work and decisions must be made through partnership.
- Experience building EHS systems, programs, metrics, vendor support, and operating rhythms for an emerging or rapidly scaling organization.
- Strong judgment and the ability to balance operational speed, technical complexity, workforce needs, compliance, and risk without defaulting to overly rigid solutions.
- Clear, credible communication skills with executives, engineers, operators, contractors, employees, and external partners, including the ability to communicate during high-pressure incidents.
- Comfort operating independently in ambiguity, with the technical depth, field orientation, pragmatism, and ownership needed to anticipate what is coming and build durable safety capability ahead of growth.

OpenAI for Financial Services is part of OpenAI's Verticals organization, which focuses on accelerating the economy and knowledge work.
We build AI products for financial institutions and the professionals who power them, from investment bankers and research analysts to investors and other financial services teams.
We combine OpenAI's models, financial data, and enterprise knowledge to help professionals research companies, analyze markets, and produce high-quality work in the tools they use every day.
We're a small, entrepreneurial team working closely with customers and partners across research, product, design, engineering, and go-to-market to bring new capabilities from idea to production.
We're looking for full-stack engineers to build new, AI-native products on top of ChatGPT Work and Codex.

section_about:
The Technical Success team helps OpenAI's customers realize meaningful and sustained value from our technology.
We partner with customers throughout their journey-from initial exploration and solution design to production implementation and organization-wide adoption.
Applied AI Engineers serve as trusted technical partners to customer executives, engineering teams, product leaders, security organizations, and transformation teams.
They combine deep technical judgment with strong customer instincts, translating frontier AI capabilities into secure, reliable systems and durable business outcomes.
We are seeking a Manager to build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting our enterprise customers.
You will be accountable for the technical success of a broad and strategically important customer portfolio.
You will help your team identify high-value opportunities, design and deploy production-grade AI systems, navigate complex technical and organizational constraints, and expand successful implementations across workflows, teams, and business units.
This role requires technical depth, people leadership, customer judgment, and operational rigor.
You should be comfortable coaching engineers through architecture and evaluation decisions, engaging directly in high-stakes customer situations, and collaborating with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Legal.
You will also help define how we serve enterprise customers at scale by developing effective coverage models, reusable implementation patterns, technical enablement, escalation mechanisms, and systems for turning field insights into high-quality product feedback.
section_responsibilities:
- Build, manage, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting large and complex enterprise customers.
- Own the quality and impact of the team's work across solution design, implementation, production readiness, adoption, and expansion.
- Coach the team through decisions involving architecture, model selection, evaluations, reliability, latency, safety, security, governance, and cost.
- Establish an operating model for prioritizing accounts and engagements according to customer needs, strategic value, technical complexity, and potential for repeatable impact.
- Serve as a senior technical escalation point during critical launches, production incidents, complex integrations, and high-stakes customer decisions.
- Partner with customer executives and technical leaders to connect implementation decisions to measurable business and operational outcomes.
- Help customers progress from experimentation to production systems and sustained adoption across their organizations.
- Partner closely with Sales and Solutions Engineering to create continuity throughout the customer lifecycle and maintain shared accountability for customer success.
- Translate customer needs and recurring implementation challenges into actionable feedback for Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and other internal teams.
- Identify scalable market patterns, distinguish them from bespoke requests, and advocate for investments that can benefit multiple customers.
- Develop reusable architectures, evaluation methods, playbooks, tooling, and enablement that improve time to value across the enterprise portfolio.
- Establish mechanisms for measuring production implementations, adoption, customer outcomes, delivery quality, team capacity, and the impact of reusable work.
- Hire thoughtfully, raise the technical and leadership bar, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning.
- Represent OpenAI with credibility and sound judgment in conversations with senior customer and internal stakeholders.
section_requirements:
- Have significant experience managing customer-facing technical teams, such as Applied AI Engineers, Solutions Architects, Forward Deployed Engineers, Customer Engineers, or Technical Account Managers.
- Have built or led teams responsible for implementing complex software, data, machine learning, or AI systems in enterprise environments.
- Maintain sufficient technical depth to evaluate architectures, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions, and coach engineers through difficult implementation decisions.
- Have experience taking AI, machine learning, or other technically complex systems from prototype to production.
- Understand production-system requirements, including reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, evaluation, and operational readiness.
- Have led teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, escalations, and rapidly evolving products or markets.
- Can translate effectively among technical details, customer needs, product strategy, and business outcomes.
- Have worked with large organizations involving multiple business units, stakeholder groups, procurement processes, or governance requirements.
- Demonstrate strong executive presence and can build trust with engineering leaders, business executives, security teams, and other senior stakeholders.
- Have designed operating models, coverage strategies, prioritization frameworks, or repeatable delivery processes for a growing technical organization.
- Are a strong cross-functional partner who can navigate disagreement directly while maintaining trust and shared accountability.
- Use data and clear principles to allocate limited resources across a large portfolio of opportunities.
- Care deeply about developing people and have a track record of coaching team members, raising performance, and building inclusive teams.
- Are energized by helping organizations adopt frontier AI responsibly and turn emerging capabilities into durable value.
RELEVANT EXPERIENCE MAY INCLUDE
- Leading teams in applied AI engineering, solutions architecture, forward-deployed engineering, professional services, technical consulting, or customer engineering.
- Implementing generative AI, machine learning, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, data platforms, or other complex enterprise technologies.
- Working with customers in semiconductors, media, entertainment, or similarly complex and technology-intensive industries.
- Supporting global customers, multi-business-unit implementations, regulated workflows, or large-scale organizational transformations.
- Building technical enablement, reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, or customer implementation methodologies.
Direct experience in these industries is not required.
We value leaders who can recognize common technical and organizational patterns while adapting their approach to different customer environments.

Our Inference team brings OpenAI's most capable research and technology to the world through our products.
We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they've never been able to before.
We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.
We're looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI's state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs.
You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.
You'll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation.
We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.
section_responsibilities:
- Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.
- Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.
- Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.
- Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.
- Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.
- Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.
section_requirements:
- Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.
- Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.
- Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.
- Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.
- Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.
- Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.
- Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.

section_about:
Security is foundational to OpenAI's mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.
The Security organization protects OpenAI's technology, people, and products by building and operating deeply technical systems that must work reliably at massive scale.
Our work underpins OpenAI's commitments around safety, privacy, and security across research, products, and emerging platforms.
The Host Assurance team exists to make bare metal and VMs dependable & scalable foundations for OpenAI: secure by default, verifiable in practice, and resilient across providers and operating models.
We operate at the trust boundary between hardware and cloud-scale orchestration, ensuring that hosts are eligible to safely run workloads with predictable security properties and auditability.
OpenAI is seeking a Software Engineer, Host Assurance to build and operate the services, APIs, and host software that establish and maintain trust in our compute infrastructure.
You will own production software from design and implementation through testing, rollout, observability, and operation.
Your work will support capabilities such as machine identity, certificate issuance and enrollment, secure bootstrap, and host attestation across bare-metal and VM environments.
Success in this role requires strong technical judgment, the ability to reason across software and host-system boundaries and learn unfamiliar parts of the stack, and a practical mindset for building systems that are secure, reliable, and usable in fast-moving production environments.
The systems you build will sit on the critical path of OpenAI's frontier infrastructure investments and will directly shape how large amounts of compute are brought online - securely, responsibly, and at global scale - underpinning long-lived commitments around privacy, security, and reliability.
You will partner closely with infrastructure, research, and confidential computing initiatives-including novel hardware platforms and emerging deployment models- to make the secure path the easiest path.
This role is well suited for engineers who enjoy working across trust services, operating systems, hardware and firmware validation, and infrastructure security, and who are excited by ambiguous, high-impact problems at the boundary of hardware and large-scale systems.
section_responsibilities:
- Design, build, and operate components of the Host Assurance platform that establish trust in both bare-metal & VM hosts before they are eligible for production use.
- Help ensure hosts are verifiably trustworthy from delivery and installation through secure bootstrap and readiness to join orchestration systems.
- Build and improve systems such as machine identity, certificate issuance and enrollment, HSM-backed or key-management-backed trust services, host attestation, measurement, and baseline verification tooling.
- Validate delivered hardware and firmware against vendor claims and continuously detect and manage drift over time.
- Eliminate insecure bootstrap patterns while preserving deployment throughput and operational reliability.
Partner with provisioning, fleet, and orchestration teams to deliver paved paths where the secure approach is the easiest approach.
- Own software components through implementation, operational readiness, launch, and ongoing operation.
Define readiness criteria, validate behavior under load and failure, establish monitoring and actionable alerts, plan staged rollouts and tested recovery procedures, and maintain runbooks.
Use production experience to improve reliability and reduce operational burden.
- Participate in production support via oncall rotation.
- Help define observable, testable security properties for host platforms and improve the telemetry and validation needed to enforce them in practice.
- Work across different deployment models and provider boundaries while maintaining a consistent bar for host trust outcomes.
section_requirements:
- Have strong software engineering experience building and operating reliable production systems at scale.
- Bring depth in distributed systems, backend or platform engineering, operating systems, or infrastructure security.
Experience with PKI, HSMs, machine identity, attestation, secure boot, or hardware security is valuable but not required.
- Can reason across services, APIs, and host software, and learn the boot, firmware, and hardware trust mechanisms relevant to your work.
Apply sound judgment to trust boundaries, correctness, and safe failure behavior.
- Have experience writing production quality code and ability to reason clearly about failure modes, operational safety, and long-term maintainability.
- Have experience supporting critical production systems at scale, such as being on-call.
- Balance rigor with pragmatism, and care about making strong security controls deployable in real-world environments.
- Are self-directed, low ego, and willing to work across disciplines to solve the most important problems.
- Enjoy building in ambiguous spaces where the architecture is still emerging, stakes are at all time high, and the future is being built.

job_title: Machine Learning Data Scientist - Consumer Forecasting
section_about:
The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company's long-term trajectory.
We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-To-Market teams to inform high-stakes decisions through rigorous data science and economic modeling.
As part of our expanding Data Science function, we're building a best-in-class Forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.
We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world.
Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI's full potential.
We're looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives.
You'll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems.
Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.
This is a highly cross-functional role, requiring technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen.
You'll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.
section_responsibilities:
- Build statistical and machine learning models to solve forecasting needs across product, finance, infrastructure, and GTM domains.
- Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.
- Develop and productionize scalable, interpretable forecasts for user growth, monetization, compute load, customer lifetime value, and profitability.
- Contribute to self-service forecasting tools and internal platforms, enabling teams across OpenAI to access and act on real-time predictions.
- Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space, such as TimeGPT, large language model extensions, causal forecasting, and hybrid approaches.
- Drive strategic insight generation by translating technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.
- Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure forecasts are well-integrated into planning processes, experimentation workflows, and executive decision-making.
section_requirements:
- Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).
- 7+ years of experience in applied data science, with deep hands-on exposure to forecasting, predictive modeling, or marketplace systems.
- Expertise in time-series forecasting techniques and practical understanding of model trade-offs across performance, explainability, and scalability.
- Proficiency in Python, SQL, and tools such as scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow, and forecasting libraries.
- Demonstrated experience with model monitoring, debugging, and long-term maintenance in production environments.
- Strong communication and storytelling skills - able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.
- Self-directed, intellectually curious, and comfortable leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.
Bonus if you have:
- Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.
- Familiarity with causal inference, Bayesian forecasting.
- Experience building agentic decision support systems.
- Passion for AI and a strong point of view on how machine learning should inform strategic decisions in fast-moving environments.

section_about:
OpenAI's Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems.
We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.
Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change.
We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.
As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes.
You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.
You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness.
Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact-not simply activity or successful demonstrations.
This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI's products evolve.
This role is based in Munich/Berlin.
section_responsibilities:
- Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.
- Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.
- Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.
- Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
- Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.
- Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.
- Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.
- Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.
section_requirements:
- Have a demonstrated track record of 5+ years of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production.
Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.
- Are fluent in both German and English
- Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems-not only program or stakeholder management.
- Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
- Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.
- Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
- Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
- Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.
- Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.
- Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.
OpenAI's Payroll team is responsible for timely and accurate processing of payroll and ensuring compliance with all statutory regulations.
At OpenAI, payroll is not a back-office function - it is mission-critical infrastructure.
We are seeking a seasoned International Payroll lead to scale and continuously improve the global payroll and payroll-support ecosystem that serves one of the fastest-growing and most technically sophisticated organizations in the world.
This role is based in our Dublin, Ireland office.
section_responsibilities:
- Lead the international payroll processing team and oversee end-to-end payroll delivery across EMEA and APAC, ensuring employees are paid accurately, on time, and in compliance with local requirements.
- Own day-to-day operations with outsourced payroll and BPO partners, including payroll calendars, inputs, reconciliations, service-level performance, quality standards, issue resolution, and escalations.
- Lead the payroll workstream for global expansion and new-country launches, including payroll registrations, in-country vendor setup, implementation, testing, systems integration, and go-live readiness.
- Partner with People, Finance, Tax, Legal, Benefits, Equity, and Treasury teams to ensure accurate upstream inputs, funding, accounting, and downstream reporting.
- Draft and maintain payroll documentation, process maps, operating procedures, and internal controls to support compliance, audit readiness, and business continuity.
- Proactively identify and resolve payroll discrepancies and employee inquiries within SLAs, determine root causes, and implement controls that prevent recurrence.
- Use data, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve controls, reduce manual work, and increase the scalability and effectiveness of international payroll operations.

- 6+ years of progressive experience in international payroll operations, preferably in a fast-paced or high-growth environment.
- Demonstrated experience leading multi-country payroll delivery across EMEA and APAC, including management of outsourced payroll or BPO providers.
- Hands-on experience supporting new-country payroll implementations, vendor onboarding, testing, and systems integrations.
- Hands-on experience using AI tools to enhance, automate, and strengthen payroll workflows and controls.
- Strong working knowledge of international payroll regulations, tax withholding, social insurance, statutory reporting, and standard payroll practices.
- Hands-on experience with Workday HCM and global payroll systems.
- Ability to independently manage priorities, take ownership of outcomes, and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Clear and concise communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, HR, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

We are hiring a Product Partnerships Manager based in Germany with primary responsibility for Germany.
You will own some of OpenAI's most important business development and partnerships in the German market while contributing to broader EMEA and international priorities.
The role is responsible for identifying, developing, and executing partnership strategies that accelerate adoption of OpenAI's products across enterprise, developer, and consumer channels.
You will identify and manage relationships with strategic product partners in Germany and on cross-border opportunities, ranging from global technology platforms to regional champions, including enterprise software vendors, telcos, cloud providers, and government-aligned organizations.
This is a deeply cross-functional role requiring close collaboration with Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, and Policy teams.
Although the role has clear accountability for Germany, team priorities may evolve, so you must be ready to take on other markets, verticals, or partnership types.
Please note that this role is based out of our Munich office, with 3 days a week required in the office.
section_responsibilities:
- Own product partnership strategy and execution for Germany, driving end-to-end partnership sourcing and delivery in the market while contributing to broader EMEA and international priorities.
- Negotiate and close strategic local and cross-border deals across commercial terms, product scope, data/privacy, brand/marketing, incentives, and expansion paths.
- Over time, lead senior partner relationships: build trust, align on joint value props, and manage complexity.
- Partner closely with Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, Policy, and regional counterparts to align roadmaps, navigate constraints, and execute partnership initiatives.
- Bring deep knowledge of Germany and a strong point of view on country and sub-region differences across EMEA, informing prioritization, positioning, and partner selection.
Apply that judgment flexibly when supporting opportunities beyond Germany or in new verticals.
- Define success metrics and use analytical judgment to assess progress, surface risks, and communicate outcomes to internal stakeholders.
section_requirements:
- 10+ years of experience in product partnerships or partnership business development within the technology industry.
- Fluency in English and German.
- Demonstrated success leading high-impact local and international partnerships involving major technology partners, including complex cross-border work.
- Deep understanding of the German market, combined with experience operating across multiple countries and international markets.
- Product-savvy with the ability to engage technical stakeholders credibly and influence product direction and roadmap tradeoffs.
- Exceptional communication, negotiation, and executive presence.
- Strong analytical instincts and comfort using data to inform decisions and communicate impact.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, highly ambiguous environment, operate both independently and collaboratively, and adapt quickly across changing markets, verticals, and partnership types.

Travel 30% of the time to support ITAV systems, technical changes, and operational readiness.

section_responsibilities:

- Build, operate, and improve AI and agentic workflows for repeatable administration, configuration checks, and troubleshooting; validate results, handle failures, and measure reductions in manual effort.
section_requirements:

- Experience configuring and troubleshooting wayfinding and conference room booking hardware, software, and room-resource integrations.

- Experience configuring and troubleshooting systems in the Q-SYS control ecosystem.
- Experience applying AV build standards, validating system performance, and maintaining clear configuration and support documentation.
- Experience using IT ticketing systems to prioritize technical escalations, communicate with users and partner teams, and meet agreed support expectations.
- Experience using basic scripting, such as Bash, Lua, Python, or JavaScript, and AI or agentic workflows to automate repeatable work, validate results, handle failures, and document how others can operate it.

section_about:
OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems.
The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.
The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.
We are seeking a White Space Manager to own the planning, coordination, and readiness of data center white-space environments.
You will connect facility delivery with compute deployment by coordinating rack layouts, electrical distribution, liquid and air cooling, structured cabling, containment, material flow, installation sequencing, and acceptance.
This role is accountable for turning completed building infrastructure into safe, usable, operations-ready data halls that can receive and activate high-density AI systems.
Travel: 50%
section_responsibilities:

- Develop installation sequences, readiness gates, turnover criteria, punch-list processes, and escalation paths across multiple workstreams.
- Partner with design, construction, commissioning, networking, hardware operations, safety, logistics, and vendors to resolve cross-system constraints.
- Verify field conditions against approved designs and maintain accurate as-built, capacity, asset, and readiness records.
- Identify risks to safe installation, energization, cooling availability, network readiness, or schedule and drive mitigations to closure.
- Create repeatable white-space standards, checklists, metrics, and operating mechanisms that scale across campuses.

- 8+ years of experience delivering or operating data center white space, critical facilities, compute deployments, or mission-critical fit-outs.
- Strong understanding of racks, power distribution, structured cabling, airflow management, liquid cooling, controls interfaces, and deployment sequencing.
- Demonstrated ownership of installation readiness, field coordination, quality, safety, and handoff across several technical disciplines.
- Experience interpreting construction documents, rack layouts, one-lines, mechanical diagrams, schedules, and commissioning records.
- Ability to manage competing dependencies and make sound decisions in an active construction or production environment.
- Strong communication with engineers, contractors, vendors, deployment teams, and operations leaders.
- Willingness to travel regularly and spend sustained time at active project sites.

section_responsibilities:

section_about:
The Mechanical Commissioning Lead owns mechanical commissioning planning, readiness, quality coordination, and test execution oversight for the project.
This role ensures mechanical systems are installed, inspected, started, balanced, controlled, and tested in a way that supports reliable integrated facility performance.
Reports to the Commissioning Project Lead and partners closely with mechanical contractors, equipment vendors, design/engineering teams, the electrical commissioning lead, controls stakeholders, and vendor field/test engineers.
Location: 100% Onsite In Texas or Georgia
section_responsibilities:
- Develop and maintain the mechanical commissioning scope, readiness criteria, inspection strategy, and discipline test execution plan.
- Review mechanical design packages, specifications, submittals, method statements, controls narratives, sequence assumptions, and testing requirements for commissionability and risk.
- Coordinate mechanical QA/QC inspections with contractors and vendor field/test engineers, including installation checks, pre-functional readiness, deficiency capture, and closeout tracking.
- Own mechanical commissioning procedure development and review, including equipment startup, functional testing, controls verification, balancing prerequisites, failure mode validation, and integrated systems testing inputs.
- Coordinate with equipment vendors on factory/site acceptance requirements, startup support, test prerequisites, documentation packages, and vendor participation during critical tests.
- Support readiness and execution for cooling, ventilation, hydronic, pumping, heat rejection, controls, and other project-specific mechanical systems.
- Lead discipline-level review of mechanical test results, deficiencies, corrective actions, retest requirements, trend logs, and acceptance evidence.
- Maintain mechanical commissioning dashboards and status inputs for the Commissioning Project Lead, including risk items, resource needs, test readiness, and issue aging.
- Partner with the Electrical Commissioning Lead on cross-discipline dependencies, including power availability, controls integration, emergency modes, heat load scenarios, and integrated testing sequences.
- Support turnover by confirming mechanical documentation, as-built evidence, test records, trend data, and outstanding issue disposition are complete and usable by operations.
section_requirements:
- 8+ years of mechanical commissioning, mechanical construction, field engineering, startup, testing, balancing coordination, controls verification, or owner representative experience on complex technical infrastructure projects.
- Strong knowledge of mechanical system startup, functional performance testing, controls interfaces, cooling or ventilation systems, hydronic systems, and equipment/vendor startup workflows as applicable to the project scope.
- Experience reviewing commissioning specifications, inspection checklists, functional test scripts, vendor startup procedures, test reports, and trend evidence.
- Ability to coordinate field execution across contractors, equipment vendors, QA/QC teams, commissioning partners, and project leadership.
- Strong practical judgment around readiness, safety, sequencing, test prerequisites, performance validation, and risk escalation.
- Comfort working in construction environments with evolving schedules and multiple parallel work fronts.
- Clear technical writing skills and discipline in maintaining logs, test evidence, issue records, and decision history.
- Ability to be present at the project site during critical mechanical installation, startup, controls checkout, functional testing, and integrated testing windows.
section_preferred:
- Owner-side or commissioning agent experience on mission-critical, industrial, manufacturing, data center, or other high-reliability facilities.
- Professional engineering, commissioning, controls, balancing, or equivalent field qualification.
- Experience with integrated systems testing and coordination between mechanical, electrical, controls, and operations teams.
- Familiarity with digital issue tracking, commissioning management platforms, schedule tools, trend tools, and field reporting workflows.
- PE license
- Commissioning certification eg.
QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP

job_title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
section_about:
The Human Flourishing team's mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing.
As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people's lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities.
The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.
Our approach has two parts.
Firstly, we measure and improve models' understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people's values and to help them achieve their long-term goals.
Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.
Our recent work includes Beneficial RL which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.
We're looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior.
You'll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.
We're especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health.
Prior experience in these domains is not required.
section_responsibilities:
- Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people's values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.
- Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.
- Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.
- Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.
- Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.
- Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.
- Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.
- Assess AI's impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.
section_requirements:
- Care deeply about helping AI improve people's lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.
- Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.
- Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.
- Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.
- Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.
- Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world-not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.
- Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.
If you're excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we'd love to hear from you.

section_about:
Training Runtime designs the core distributed runtime that powers everything from early research experiments to frontier-scale model runs.
We build robust, scalable, high performance components to support our distributed training workloads.
Our priorities are to maximize the productivity of our researchers and our hardware, accelerating progress towards AGI.
Within Training Runtime, the Runtime Foundations team develops the distributed OS responsible for orchestrating the large numbers of processes that make up modern training workloads and providing all necessary observability and resilience to operate in frontier scale environments.
Our runtime sits beneath training frameworks and on top of research infrastructure, ensuring jobs run reliably across massive clusters while maintaining performance, stability, and observability.
Success for us is measured by both system reliability and researcher velocity - enabling ideas to scale from experiments to production training runs.
As a Training Runtime: Runtime Foundations Engineer, you will work on the software that ties thousands of computers together and exposes them as a unified system.
This system has to serve individual researchers running multiple parallel experiments, as well as our largest training runs spanning 100's of thousands and even millions of machines and accelerators.
This requires easy to use, introspectable systems that can promote a fast debugging and development cycle, as well as relentless optimization for scale while maintaining stability and performance throughout.
You will work primarily in Codex + Rust, building high-performance asynchronous systems with a strong emphasis on performance, correctness, resilience, and scalability.
Working at this scale and at the frontier of AI development poses novel challenges.
We support many different types of research, and the problems you will be working on are highly ambiguous and require a superb ability to jump into novel domains, understand user problems, and demonstrate both strong design judgment and proficient execution to advance our programs.
We're looking for people who love optimizing an end-to-end platform, understanding high-performance architectures to maximize both local and distributed performance across our supercomputers.
We're looking for engineers excited by the rapid pace of responding to the dynamic and evolving needs of our training runtime and compute stack.
section_responsibilities:
- Work across our Python and Rust stack
- Design, build, and maintain software to orchestrate and monitor machine learning workloads on our largest supercomputers
- Profile and optimize our software stack to support computation orchestration at frontier scale
- Improve reliability, observability, and fault tolerance for long-running jobs
- Debug complex distributed systems issues across large clusters
- Respond to the changing shapes and needs of the ML systems to enable our researchers
section_requirements:
- Have experience developing distributed systems
- Enjoy understanding how large systems behave and fail at scale
- Love being both a developer and an operator
- Care deeply about performance, correctness, and reliability
- Have strong software engineering skills and are proficient in Rust or another systems programming language (e.g.
C++)
- Have solid Linux knowledge, and are comfortable with systems-level debugging, performance analysis, and memory profiling
- Are comfortable and experienced in developing asynchronous and concurrent systems
- Like high-ownership environments with light process and strong engineering agency

section_about:
OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organization is positioned for long-term success as we pursue our mission.
The Strategic Sourcing & Procurement team enables OpenAI to scale responsibly, securely, and at speed by helping teams choose the right external partners, structure strong commercial agreements, and build resilient supplier ecosystems.
We work at the intersection of innovation and execution, partnering closely with product and engineering leaders across the company to turn rapidly evolving needs into scalable, compliant, and economically sound solutions.
We are hiring a Sourcing Manager to keep vendor and partnership workflows moving from intake through onboarding, review and approval.
You will coordinate a portfolio of agreed sourcing requests across multiple OpenAI product areas, bringing structure, accuracy and dependable follow-through.
You will work with senior sourcing owners and cross-functional partners.
Senior owners retain responsibility for strategic supplier selection, negotiations and sensitive commercial or data-rights decisions.
section_responsibilities:
- Run high-velocity, mid-complexity deals end-to-end: from vendor strategy and RFPs through negotiation, security review, contracting, and go-live.
- Coordinate supplier onboarding, collect required documents and track dependencies through completion.
- Drive approval follow-through with Legal, Security, Privacy, Finance and other reviewers.
- Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure external vendors can support new product launches without blocking delivery or increasing risk.
- Structure contracts and pricing models that preserve optionality, support rapid scaling, and minimize long-term lock-in and switching costs.
- Maintain accurate deal records, status updates, decisions and next actions.
- Support sourcing requests, renewals, evaluations and change orders.
- Act as the control plane between fast-moving product teams and external dependencies, ensuring speed without sacrificing governance, compliance, or economics.
section_requirements:
- 5+ year experience leading technology partnerships, sourcing, or commercial negotiations in a high-growth, product-driven environment.
- Strong cross-functional leadership-able to align Product, Engineering, Legal, Security, and Finance around complex, high-stakes decisions.
- Comfort operating in regulated or high-risk domains (payments, identity, data, financial or health-adjacent infrastructure).
- A track record of negotiating commercial, technical, and data-driven agreements with technology vendors.
- The ability to move fast in ambiguity while maintaining commercial discipline, compliance, and risk awareness.
- Strong analytical skills to evaluate pricing models, volume ramps, FX exposure, and vendor risk in the context of revenue and product growth.
- An ownership mindset-you independently drive deals, resolve blockers, and close outcomes that materially impact product launches and revenue.
- A desire to accelerate OpenAI's mission by enabling better vendor partnerships, faster launches, and more effective execution at scale.
